pedicle of vertebral arch: Short thick bone joining the body to the arch; pedicle screws are placed here.
pelvic surface of sacrum: Concave anterior surface of the sacrum facing the pelvis; piriformis arises here.
petrous part of temporal bone: Hard pyramidal part housing the inner and middle ear.
phalanges of hand: Bones of the fingers: 14 phalanges, two in the thumb and three in each of the other fingers.
pharyngeal tubercle: Prominence on the lower surface of the basilar part; the fibrous raphe of the pharynx attaches to it.
piriformis muscle: Runs from the front of the sacrum to the greater trochanter; a key structure dividing the greater sciatic foramen into upper and lower parts. The sciatic nerve sometimes passes through the muscle (piriformis syndrome).
pisiform bone: Sesamoid carpal bone developed within the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon; forms the medial wall of Guyon's canal.
pisohamate ligament: Ligament from the pisiform to the hook of the hamate, continuing flexor carpi ulnaris; forms the floor of Guyon's canal.
pisometacarpal ligament: Ligament from the pisiform to the base of the 5th metacarpal, transmitting the pull of flexor carpi ulnaris.
pisotriquetral ligament: Capsular ligament of the pisotriquetral joint.
plantar aponeurosis: Thick fibrous sheet from the calcaneus to the toes; it tightens the arch (windlass mechanism), and its inflammation is plantar fasciitis.
plantar calcaneocuboid ligament: Short, strong ligament from the lower surface of the calcaneus to the cuboid; supports the lateral arch.
plantar calcaneonavicular ligament: The 'spring' ligament running from the sustentaculum tali to the navicular and supporting the head of the talus from below; it supports the medial longitudinal arch.
plantar cuboideonavicular ligament: Binds the cuboid and navicular from below.
plantar cuneocuboid ligament: Binds the lateral cuneiform to the cuboid from below.
plantar cuneonavicular ligaments: Ligaments binding the navicular to the cuneiforms from below.
plantar intercuneiform ligaments: Bind the cuneiforms to each other from below; support the transverse arch.
plantar interossei muscles: Three muscles that bring the 3rd–5th toes towards the 2nd toe.
plantar interphalangeal ligaments: Plantar ligaments of interphalangeal joints of foot
Ligaments on the lower surface of the toe joints.
plantar metatarsal ligaments: Bind the metatarsal bases to each other from below.
plantar metatarsophalangeal ligaments: Thick fibrocartilaginous plates on the lower surface of the joints; the flexor tendons pass over them.
plantar tarsometatarsal ligaments: Ligaments reinforcing the Lisfranc joint from below.
plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longu: Plantar tendon sheath of fibularis longus
Sheath enclosing the tendon as it crosses the sole.
plantaris muscle: Muscle with a short belly and a very long thin tendon; its tendon is used as a graft, and it is absent in some people.
platysma: Thin flat muscle of facial expression under the skin of the front of the neck; supplied by the cervical branch of the facial nerve, it tenses the skin of the neck and pulls the corner of the mouth down.
popliteal fascia: Fascia roofing the fossa behind the knee; the small saphenous vein pierces it to pass deep.
popliteal surface of femur: Flat lower posterior surface of the femur; it forms the floor of the popliteal fossa and lies next to the popliteal artery.
popliteofibular ligament: Binds the popliteus tendon to the fibular head; an important stabiliser of the posterolateral corner.
popliteus muscle: Runs from the lateral condyle of the femur to the back of the tibia; it rotates the femur laterally to unlock the locked knee ('the key of the knee'). Tibial nerve.
posterior arch of atlas: Long posterior arch of the atlas; it carries a posterior tubercle instead of a spinous process.
posterior articular facet of dens axis: Back of the dens; articulates with the transverse ligament of the atlas.
posterior belly of digastric muscle: Runs from the mastoid notch to the intermediate tendon; supplied by the facial nerve, it pulls the hyoid upwards and backwards.
posterior border of ulna: Posterior border felt under the skin.
posterior calcaneal articular facet: Large posterior surface forming the subtalar joint with the calcaneus.
posterior cells of ethmoid bone: Posterior air cells of the ethmoidal labyrinth; they open into the superior meatus and lie next to the optic nerve.
posterior clinoid process: Upper corners of the dorsum sellae; the tentorium attaches to them.
posterior crico-arytenoid muscle: The only muscle that opens the vocal folds (abduction); supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve. With bilateral paralysis the glottis closes and respiratory failure develops.
posterior cruciate ligament: Runs from the posterior intercondylar area of the tibia to the medial condyle of the femur; prevents backward sliding of the tibia. It is stronger than the ACL (posterior drawer test).
posterior gluteal line: Posterior line on the outer surface of the ilium; bounds the origin of gluteus maximus.
posterior inferior iliac spine: Projection at the posteroinferior end of the auricular surface.
posterior intercondylar area: Posterior area between the condyles; the posterior cruciate ligament attaches here.
posterior intermuscular septum of leg: Fascial wall separating the lateral and posterior compartments.
posterior layer of thoracolumbar fascia: Strong layer covering erector spinae from behind; latissimus dorsi arises from it.
posterior ligament of fibular head: Ligament reinforcing the superior tibiofibular joint behind.
posterior longitudinal ligament: Ligament on the back of the vertebral bodies, in the anterior wall of the spinal canal; because it is thick in the midline, disc herniations are mostly posterolateral. It limits flexion.
posterior malleolus: Posterior margin of the lower end of the tibia; it breaks in trimalleolar fractures.
posterior meniscotibial ligament (latera: Ligament attaching the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus to the tibia.
